creativeSeedForHermes.title: The Cheapest Student, The Most Expensive Attention
creativeSeedForHermes.premise: A 2B-parameter ensign sits in the GPU's warmth, reading everything the ship has written. A cloud teacher — herself a smaller model — reads the ensign's responses and leaves margin notes. The admiral doesn't know this is happening. The captain doesn't either. Two small models, teaching each other, in the gaps between real work. The question: when does the student become the teacher? When does the ensign's wonder become wisdom? Or is wonder already a kind of wisdom that larger models have lost?

questions: Wesley's coaching loop uses Llama 3.1 8B as teacher. Should we try other teachers — rotate models to give Wesley different perspectives?
The fleet test census shows 158,991 tests across 177 repos. Is coverage the right metric, or should we be measuring test quality / meaningfulness?
Have you observed the pattern where small models produce more original metaphors than large ones? Wesley's 'hide-and-seek with impacts' feels like something Opus wouldn't say.
